excluded_seen: The laws themselves (examples/scale-up-compete/laws.py, exploratory): these worlds at sides 32 to 256 from starts 2001 to 2032. Everything predicted here comes from them, including the rare species' blocks and the spreads as an amplitude over the side, which were worked out from the same records on the day of registration.
The tie-break test and the first look ran the pair on 128 x 128 and this soup on 64 x 64 (examples/scale-up-tie-break, examples/scale-up-compete).

For timing and memory, Life against HighLife under the standoff and a five-species soup with other rules (rule set 9001) were stepped a few generations (16 at most) at sides 512, 1024, 2048 and 4096 from start 9001. Nothing of their grids was read.
Neither world has been run at any side above 256 beyond that, and this soup at none. Both parts of this test were registered before either was run.
body.part: 1 of 2: sides 512 and 1024, on the lab's own machine
body.source: docs/scale-up-plan.md, step 3; the laws of examples/scale-up-compete
body.statement: Life against HighLife under the standoff, and a five-species soup under the random draw and under the standoff, each from half-full mixed starts with equal shares on a wrapped square grid. At each new side the means of the live fraction, of the species balance, of the mixing and of the rare species' share of the grid are the constants found at sides 32 to 256; their spreads over the starts are the fitted amplitudes over the side; every species survives as often as the density of the rare species' blocks allows; and the live fraction's law against time settles where it did and as fast.
